description: Sotto v3: speaking up when the room needs it. Sotto answers what the room wonders aloud (open questions it can look up) with a short sourced spoken answer at a real pause, keeps a conversation open for follow-ups without the wake word, asks one probing question at decision points, offers longer contributions ask-first, moves corrections to screen, and lets the room steer it by voice. Spark gates interjections; Glimmer gates research ideas. Full spec: tasks/prd-sotto-v3.md (wins over tasks/prd-sotto-v2.md and tasks/prd-sotto-core.md).

userStories.title: Gate per path: Spark for interjections, Glimmer for research
userStories.description: As the system, I want each judgment made by the model that can make it in time.
acceptanceCriteria: Interjection candidates (CandidateGate) are gated by Muse Spark by default; research ideas (ResearchGate) stay on Glimmer, falling back to Spark. --gate on the eval and e2e can still force either path for A/B runs
tasks/decisions.md records the split and its measured basis (Glimmer gate 24-34 s vs 12-29 s windows; V2-021 e2e delivered planted moments 31.9 s and 50.1 s late; Spark 9/9 vs 7/9 moment recall)
npm run e2e: the planted moments in moment-contradiction and research-business-idea are delivered inside their windows (report delivery time vs deadline for each)
The eval report shows median gate latency per path
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Noticing what the room is wondering (open_question)
userStories.description: As the system, I need to tell a real open question Sotto can answer from a rhetorical one, an already-answered one, and one only the group can answer.
acceptanceCriteria: New candidate type open_question: asked or wondered aloud to the room (not to Sotto), not answered in the turns since, and answerable by lookup (web, later the knowledge folder). Not: questions only the group can answer, rhetorical questions, decisions
unanswered_question keeps questions only the group can answer (screen only); research_hook keeps 'we should look into X' requests (research gate as today)
The candidate carries question (cleaned), askedBy and sourceTurnId
Observer prompt defines open_question with positive and negative examples, including rhetorical and decision questions

New fixture rhetorical-questions (2-3 min, Craig and EJ): at least four rhetorical/decision questions, one question asked and answered by a person within two turns, one genuine open question (positive control); rendered, captured, added to the eval set
Integration test (events replay): offsite-plan's drive-time question yields an open_question; rhetorical-questions yields exactly one (the positive control)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Fast path from question to answer
userStories.description: As the system, when the room wonders something Sotto can look up, I want the answer ready while it still matters.
acceptanceCriteria: An open_question skips the 2-minute planner and starts research immediately, gated by Spark (answerable by search, useful now?), counted against the research budget (V2-012), deduplicated against earlier ideas and packets

The research runner adds packet.spokenAnswer: one or two sentences answering the question directly, written to be heard (sensible rounding, no URLs), grounded in the sources; zero sources means no spokenAnswer
The integration test checks with the judge that spokenAnswer answers the question asked (an overnight packet answered about AGM software for a question about meeting assistants)
Target: median <= 25 s from question turn final to packet ready, recorded as questionToPacketMs in research.jsonl on the e2e fixtures
Unit tests: fast path vs planner path, shared budget, dedupe
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Speaking the answer to the room
userStories.description: As a user, when we wondered something aloud and Sotto found the answer, I want it to tell us briefly, at a natural moment, without talking over anyone.
acceptanceCriteria: When a spokenAnswer is ready, Sotto waits for a real pause (no open turn and >= SPEAK_PAUSE_MS, default 1500, since the last speechEnd), then speaks it attributed to the asker ('EJ, on the drive time: about two hours fifteen from the city.')
Still-open check right before speaking: one quick Spark call over the turns since the question (answered by a person, or clearly closed?); if closed, card only; result logged

Never over anyone: a speechStart after the decision to speak but before first audio cancels the utterance and retries at the next real pause; barge-in (V2-007) handles anyone who starts once it is speaking
Expiry: not spoken within 90 s of ready or after 6 more final turns -> card only
The research card still appears with sources; the spoken line appears in the transcript as Sotto's (V2-008a)
Counts against the frequency budget and cooldown (V2-017); muted or boldness cautious -> card only
timing.jsonl records spoken_contribution with kind answer, questionToSpeechMs, pauseWaitMs, stillOpen, cancelledForSpeech and barged-in
Offline simulated-clock tests: waits for a real pause, cancels when speech starts before audio, still-open closed -> card, expiry, budget, muted, cautious
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (replay offsite-plan with the null audio sink: the spoken line appears in the transcript and the card shows sources)

userStories.title: Follow-ups without the wake word
userStories.description: As a user, once I've asked Sotto something and it has answered, I want to keep talking to it without saying 'Sotto' each time, and I want it to notice when we've gone back to talking among ourselves.
acceptanceCriteria: After Sotto finishes speaking an answer (addressed, unprompted, or an accepted offer) a follow-up window opens; 'Sotto is listening' stays visible in a distinct 'in conversation' style

Each final turn in the window is classified by Spark with Sotto's last answer and recent turns as context: to_sotto (a follow-up), to_room (humans resumed), or closing ('great, thanks'); may share code with the V2-008 address and V2-007 command classifiers
to_sotto -> answered like a wake question and the window stays open from the end of that answer; to_room or closing -> the window closes silently
When unsure, close: an ambiguous turn is treated as to_room
The window also closes after 20 s with no final turn or after 2 consecutive human-to-human turns; any person may follow up
Barge-in during an answer works as today; a barge-in new_question counts as to_sotto
timing.jsonl logs followup_window opened/closed with reason, and each classification with kind and latencyMs
Offline simulated-clock tests: follow-up answered, humans resuming closes, 'thanks' closes, timeout, two human turns, ambiguous -> closed

New fixture followups (2-3 min, Craig and EJ): a wake question, two follow-ups without the name, then the pair resume with a question addressed to each other by name (must NOT be answered), then a fresh wake question; rendered, captured, in the eval set; answered-when-not-addressed counts as a false answer, gate 0
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (replay followups: the in-conversation indicator appears after the answer and clears when the humans resume)

userStories.title: Probing questions at decision points
userStories.description: As a user, when we're about to lock in a decision with an unexamined risk, I want Sotto to ask one specific question instead of telling us we're wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: Corrections become questions everywhere: card text for contradiction, untested_assumption and dropped_thread is a specific question tied to what was said; the observer prompt names generic coach-speak ('Have you considered your audience?') as a bad example
New signal decision_closing: the group is settling something ('OK, let's go with six gardens', 'so we're agreed on Saturday'); the observer flags it on the final turn

Spoken only at a decision point: if a decision_closing turn relates to an open contradiction or untested_assumption candidate that passed the gate, Sotto speaks one probing question at the next real pause under the V3-004 rules (real pause, never over anyone, still-open check, expiry 20 s); no relevant candidate -> nothing spoken
At most one spoken probing question per 10 minutes; counts against the frequency budget; cautious or muted -> card only; the room's quieter (V3-006) applies once built
Logged as spoken_contribution with kind probe, the decision turn and the candidate

Fixtures: planted decision moments, some with a real unexamined risk (expectedLevel speak) and some without; integration test (events replay): the risky decision gets a question, the safe decision and brainstorm get none
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Corrections go on screen
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto's corrections available but never forced on the room.
acceptanceCriteria: contradiction, factual_error, untested_assumption, dropped_thread and unanswered_question are cards only in every mode, except a probing question at a decision point (V3-013) and a verified factual_error at boldness bold (one sentence under the V3-004 rules)
The interjection eval gates are unchanged (they measure deliveries, not speech)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Eval for unprompted speech
userStories.description: As the developer, I need to measure unprompted speech the way the interjection eval measures cards.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixture moments gain expectedLevel speak for open questions and risky decisions Sotto should speak to (offsite-plan drive time, the rhetorical-questions positive control, V3-013's planted risky decisions)

Scoring: a speak moment is caught if Sotto speaks something the judge matches to it, at a real pause, before any human answered it, within its window; false speech is any unprompted utterance on brainstorm, no-wake or rhetorical-questions that matches no moment; answered-when-not-addressed on followups is a false answer
Gates: speak recall >= 0.6; zero false speech; zero false answers on followups; 100% of spoken contributions at a real pause; existing gates unchanged
Report adds a spoken-contributions table: moment, text, questionToSpeechMs, pause wait, still-open result
The e2e (real time) applies the same scoring to its fixtures, since only real time shows real latency
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: HUMAN CHECKPOINT: live test of speaking up
userStories.description: As the team, we need to hear whether Sotto speaking up unprompted is welcome before tuning further.
acceptanceCriteria: The loop does not start this story until tasks/checkpoint-speaking.md exists (ralph.sh enforces this)

A human runs a ~10-minute live session (two people if possible, a phone voice as stand-in otherwise): wonder aloud about lookup-able things, ask rhetorical questions, answer one yourselves before Sotto does, settle a risky and a safe decision, ask Sotto something and follow up twice without its name then return to each other, and say 'not now' once; plus the deferred V2-008 checks (side talk during speech, crosstalk)
tasks/checkpoint-speaking.md records each unprompted contribution (what, welcome?, timing, false or late) and 'Would you leave it on?', ending RESULT: PASS or RESULT: FAIL with notes
If RESULT: PASS: set passes true and summarize the findings in notes
If RESULT: FAIL: fix the listed problems in this iteration, commit, rename the file to tasks/checkpoint-speaking-fail-<n>.md (so the loop stops again for a retest), and leave passes false with notes

userStories.title: Asking first for anything longer
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to offer longer contributions and let us decide.
acceptanceCriteria: A packet from the planner or a research_hook (not an open question with a short answer) is offered aloud at a real pause in one sentence ('I've got a quick rundown on competitors if you want it'); the card appears at the same time

For 10 s after the offer, the next final turn from anyone is classified by Spark as yes / no / unrelated with no wake word needed; yes -> the V2-015 spoken briefing from that packet; no or unrelated -> nothing more, the card stays
At most one open offer at a time; offers count against the frequency budget
Logged as spoken_contribution with kind offer and its outcome
Offline tests: yes, no, unrelated, timeout, a second offer while one is open
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: The room can turn Sotto down, or up
userStories.description: As a user, I want to steer how forward Sotto is just by talking to it.
acceptanceCriteria: During or within 15 s after an unprompted contribution, an addressed 'stop' / 'not now' / 'too much' (command classification gains quieter) stops speech and lowers frequency one step for the session; 'Sotto, you can jump in more' (louder) raises it one step
Header controls reflect the change and it is saved in session settings; a short on-screen note says what changed
A barge-in 'stop' during an unprompted contribution counts as quieter; during an answer to a question it does not
Logged in timing.jsonl
Offline tests
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: The hello sets expectations
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to tell us up front that it may chime in, and how to stop it.
acceptanceCriteria: server/prompts/hello.md adds one sentence: Sotto may chime in when the group wonders something it can look up, and 'Sotto, not now' quiets it
The hello stays under about 20 s spoken (measured from a real render)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Offering ideas when the group is stuck
userStories.description: As a user, when we're going around in circles, I want Sotto to offer a few ideas, only if we want them.
acceptanceCriteria: New candidate type stall: the same question or problem revisited across >= 3 turns without progress, or explicit 'I don't know'/'we're stuck' with no new idea following; defined with negative examples (a normal pause, thinking aloud once)
A stall is offered, never volunteered ('Want a few ideas on the name?') using the V3-005 ask-first flow; yes -> up to three short ideas spoken in ~20 s plus a card
At most one stall offer per 10 minutes
Integration test (events replay) on a fixture with a planted stall: detected and offered; brainstorm produces no stall offer
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: The knowledge folder (stretch)
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to answer from our own files, not just the web.
acceptanceCriteria: A folder (KNOWLEDGE_DIR, default knowledge/, git-ignored) of .md, .txt and .csv files is indexed at session start (plain-text search is fine)
The research runner gets a search_knowledge tool next to web_search and cites files as sources ('file: customers.csv')
fixtures/knowledge-demo/ holds a small, clearly labelled fictional company (customer list with renewal dates, price sheet, notes) for the demo and tests
Integration test: an open question about a customer's renewal date is answered from the folder with a file citation
Typecheck passes
